From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Intro / call recap — HIPAA scope questions

Hi Daniel — great speaking with you and thanks for the clear list. Attaching a concise summary and next steps. High level answers below; attaching a one‑page mapping and our standard BAA template for your legal team.

1) SOC 2: Redwood has a Type II report (Security + Availability) current through 2026-09. I'll share the AOC and a redacted report under an NDA if needed.

2) BAA: Yes, we provide a standard BAA. It is supported for Redwood Hosted (our managed API) and Redwood Dedicated (customer-dedicated GPU pools). For our Private on-prem package we offer a BAA addendum that accounts for customer-managed infra — legal prefers a short intake form for private install specifics.

3) PHI handling / boundaries: we recommend the following patterns depending on your integration: 
  - Hosted / Dedicated: PHI may be sent to the model but is not stored persistently by default. We provide optional prefix/KV cache encryption and automatic prefix scrubbing rules. Logs and request traces can be configured to omit raw prompt text.
  - Private (VPC or on-prem): gives you full control over storage and network boundaries; Redwood's control plane can be configured to limit telemetry retention.

Recommended for MedPath given your timeline: start with Redwood Dedicated (predictable throughput + BAA available) for pilot, and evaluate Private if legal requires full control of hosting.

Action items from Redwood: 
- Send AOC + redacted SOC 2 (by EOD 12/10) — Marcus will own this.
- Share standard BAA + short summary of PHI controls (attached) — Kimberly.
- Kick off vendor security questionnaire (we'll send a link to your security alias) — Priya will own the questionnaire intake.

I'll also include a HubSpot link to the deal and a Drive doc with the one-page mapping. Let me know if you want a quick follow-up call this week.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales — Healthcare Vertical
Redwood Inference

Hi Kimberly,

Quick notes from security: we reviewed the summary you sent. Two clarifying questions before we start the full questionnaire: 

1) Can you confirm whether model weights or derivatives are ever persisted outside GPU memory in Redwood Hosted? In other words, is there any long-term model‑level telemetry that could include PHI?
2) For Dedicated deployments, who is responsible for disk encryption configuration — Redwood or the customer? We need precise language for our procurement team.

If you can provide short answers to these two points and the SOC 2 AOC, we'll start the questionnaire and expect to complete it by 12/17.

Thanks,
Asha R. (on behalf of MedPath Security)
Infosec Manager
MedPath Diagnostics
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: MedPath Security <security@medpath.com>, Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@medpath.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intro / call recap — HIPAA scope questions

Hi Asha / team — quick answers inline: 

1) Model persistence: Redwood Hosted does not persist model weights or per‑request model derivatives to disk as part of normal inference flows. Transient caches live in GPU memory; optional persistent KV caches can be enabled by customers and are encrypted at rest when enabled. We will include this language in the SOC 2 AOC redaction pack.

2) Disk encryption for Dedicated: Redwood configures and manages encryption-at-rest for any storage we control in a Redwood-Managed Dedicated offering. For Dedicated deployments where the customer attaches their own storage, the customer is responsible for their encryption configuration; we document the expected controls in the BAA addendum.

Next steps: Marcus will drop the AOC link to the Drive doc and Priya will send the vendor questionnaire URL by EOD. Would you prefer DocuSign for the BAA or a tracked Word document first?

Thanks — looking forward to moving this to procurement.

Kim
